def: An ordered list of numbers that can also be drawn as an arrow from the origin; the basic object of linear algebra.
The length of a vector; the Euclidean (L2) norm is the square root of the sum of squared components.
A vector of length 1, obtained by dividing a vector by its norm so that only its direction remains.
The sum of products of matching components, equal to the product of the two lengths and the cosine of the angle between them.
Perpendicular: two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero.
The dot product of two vectors divided by the product of their lengths, which compares direction only and lies between -1 and 1.
Dividing a vector by its norm so that its length becomes 1.
The part of a vector that lies along a given direction, found by scaling that direction by (x . w)/(w . w).
What is left of a vector after subtracting its projection; it is orthogonal to the direction projected onto.
A sum of vectors each multiplied by a scalar, such as c1 x + c2 y.
A vector produced by a trained model for an item such as a word or sentence so that similar items get similar vectors.
